haiku-low.q1: Its document is deleted from search. Archived status is treated as a delete action, so the product is no longer searchable.
haiku-low.q2: The older change is rejected by the versioned write as stale, counted in stale_conflicts_total and treated as success. The newer version stays.
haiku-low.q3: It retries unresolved items with backoff from 1 s to a 60 s cap, with no retry limit. It pauses partitions, keeps polling, never skips ahead, and alerts after 2 minutes.
haiku-low.q4: The event, target index and error go to catalog.products.dlq and an alert is raised. Processing continues, and that product stays stale until the DLQ item is fixed and replayed by hand.
haiku-low.q5: At 50 GB ops drops the slot and changes since then are lost, so the live index goes stale. Recover by recreating search_slot, restarting Debezium, confirming events flow, then running a rebuild.
haiku-low.q6: One atomic alias request removes the old index and adds products_vN. The gate must pass: lag under 5 s for 3 checks in a row and document count within 0.5% of active rows.
haiku-low.q7: Live progress is in Kafka consumer-group offsets, committed only after every batch item is resolved. Rebuild progress is in the compacted rebuild-state topic, with last_id checkpointed after each acked page.
haiku-low.q8: It resumes from the last committed offsets and replays the batch. This is harmless because writes are idempotent, so nothing is lost.
haiku-low.q9: Events are applied only after the load ends, replayed from T0 minus 10 min in commit order per product, so no resurrection occurs. Events the snapshot already reflects are stale or overwritten harmlessly.
haiku-low.q10: Bulk-copy documents carry version S, the pg_current_wal_lsn value read just before the snapshot opened.
haiku-low.q11: The old index keeps its own consumer group and old mapper, so it receives every change for 48 hours. The hold ends after 48 hours: old group stopped, offsets deleted, old index deleted, stage RETIRED.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for search during partial failure beyond this: the gate not being met keeps the old index live and nothing switches. A failed gate over 1 hour or abandonment deletes the half-built products_vN.

sonnet.q1: The change becomes a delete action (archived status maps to delete, enforcing the search rule that only active rows appear). The delete carries the commit_lsn version; a delete of a missing document (404) counts as success.
sonnet.q2: The older change has a lower version (commit_lsn), so the index returns a version conflict for that document. The indexer counts it in stale_conflicts_total, treats it as success, and the newer data stays; nothing is overwritten.
sonnet.q3: It retries only the unresolved items with backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... capped at 60 s) with no retry limit. It never moves to the next batch and does not commit offsets. It pauses partitions but keeps calling poll() to avoid a rebalance, and alerts if this lasts over 2 minutes.
sonnet.q4: The event, target index and error are published to catalog.products.dlq, an alert is raised, and processing carries on (offsets are committed). That product stays stale until the DLQ item is fixed and replayed by hand; one change is lost per DLQ item.
sonnet.q5: At 20 GB retained WAL on search_slot, on-call is paged. At 50 GB ops drops the slot, and changes since the drop are lost, so the live index becomes stale. Recovery is a full rebuild: recreate search_slot, restart Debezium, confirm events flow, then start the rebuild (the snapshot recovers the gap).
sonnet.q6: The search API queries the alias products. After one atomic alias update (remove old index, add products_vN), queries use the new index. Before that, the gate must pass: lag under 5 s for 3 checks in a row (checked every 30 s) AND document count within 0.5% of the active row count on the primary.
sonnet.q7: Live path progress is stored in Kafka consumer-group offsets (group indexer-<index name>), committed only after every item in the batch is resolved (acknowledged, stale, or sent to the DLQ). Rebuild progress is stored in the compacted topic catalog.products.rebuild-state (last_id checkpointed after each acknowledged page).
sonnet.q8: It resumes from the last committed offsets and replays the batch. This is harmless because writes are idempotent (versioned, replays count as stale or are applied the same).
sonnet.q9: They are not applied during the copy. After the load finishes, a group indexer-products_vN starts from Kafka offsets at T0 minus 10 min and replays the stream on top using the same code as the live path. Events already reflected in the snapshot have version at most S, so they count as stale or are overwritten in order by later events. Events stay in Kafka (7-day retention).
sonnet.q10: version = S, the value of pg_current_wal_lsn read just before the snapshot opened (a new S2 is stored per chunk if a snapshot is reopened after connection loss or failover).
sonnet.q11: The old index keeps its own consumer group and old mapper, so it still receives every change during a 48-hour hold; rollback means checking the old group's lag is under 5 s, then moving the alias back atomically. After 48 hours, the old group is stopped, its offsets deleted, and the old index deleted (stage RETIRED), ending rollback ability.
sonnet.q12: Search is unaffected: the alias still points at the old index, which stays live, since the new index is not behind the alias until the switch. If the gate fails for over 1 hour or the rebuild is abandoned, alert, keep the old index live and delete the half-built products_vN. A restarted rebuild can instead resume from the state topic; failures in the load pause or reopen the snapshot with no data lost.
